Window inspected: measured latest durable autoheal incidents plus latest 24h autoheal action history, trends, transitions, and uptime on 2026-05-15. Signal counts: incidents latest reported 34 open incidents: 24 host_integrity, 9 unclean_boot, 1 autoheal_failure; source counts included host-kernel-error-signals 10, host-kernel-module-drift 6, host-package-state 7, system-boot-history 8, system-mce-recent 2, system-pstore-evidence 1. Autoheal trends over 24h reported totalEvents=34482, okEvents=26661, warningEvents=4773, criticalEvents=3048, uptimePercentage=77.31860100922219. Signal picked: autoheal scenario restart heal-loop / slow-restart pattern. Evidence: latest 50 autoheal actions had 10 successes and 40 failures; failures grouped as 32 action timed out, 7 exit status 1, 1 API start script not found. Failure concentration: scenario-test-genie 15, scenario-app-monitor 7, scenario-web-console 6, app-issue-tracker 3, prd-control-tower 3. Lifecycle lock examples: web-console and agent-manager restart outputs showed 'Scenario restart blocked by concurrent invocation' with held pids. Transitions over 24h showed 50 status changes led by web-console 8, browser-automation-studio 6, vrooli-orphans 6, agent-manager 4, ecosystem-manager 4, with repeated ok->critical and critical->ok pairs. Pattern observed: autoheal is spending most restart actions on timeout or lifecycle-lock failures while the same scenarios later transition healthy, so retries appear poorly reconciled with in-flight lifecycle work and slow successful starts. Hypothesized root cause: restart action timeout/backoff policy does not sufficiently detect in-progress lifecycle locks or reconcile scenario health after timeout before retrying. Measurement plan: track restart attempt result, duration, lock-holder pid, post-timeout scenario status, and next transition time per scenario; alert only when repeated failures occur without a subsequent healthy transition inside the configured grace window. Missing telemetry: first-class aggregate action-loop summary by scenario/error/post-timeout recovery would reduce manual jq over actions history/transitions. Decisions: raised runtime-health-finding proposal dec-1778888027214366413 for lock-aware restart backoff/reconciliation.

Slice audited: cli-setup (prompt-manager setup lifecycle, scenario service CLI install metadata, cli-core installer/stale-checker, Windows/Unix install wrappers, and Makefile setup entrypoint). Top finding: prompt-manager's Windows CLI installer wrapper is not at parity with Unix or peer scenario wrappers. Evidence: scenarios/prompt-manager/cli/install.sh delegates to packages/cli-core/install.sh with --manifest scenarios/prompt-manager/.vrooli/service.json; scenarios/prompt-manager/.vrooli/service.json declares cli.install for linux/darwin and windows plus cli.freshness.inputs [cli/**, .vrooli/service.json]; packages/cli-core/install.sh reads cli.freshness.inputs from the manifest and forwards --manifest, --context-root, and --freshness-input to cli-installer; packages/cli-core/install.ps1 supports -Manifest and forwards --manifest, but does not read manifest freshness inputs; scenarios/prompt-manager/cli/install.ps1 calls the shared PowerShell installer with only ModulePath and -Name, omitting -Manifest. Peer wrappers such as scenarios/data-backup-manager/cli/install.ps1 and many others pass -ModulePath, -Name, and -Manifest. Impact: Windows prompt-manager installs can lack the installed sibling manifest used by cliutil.LoadRuntimeManifest and can be built from a different freshness contract than NewStandardScenarioApp's runtime stale checker, creating stale-check warnings or rebuild loops on Windows. Measured checks: go test ./cmd/cli-installer and go test ./cliapp passed under packages/cli-core; go test ./cliutil failed in existing TestDetermineAPIBaseKeepsGenericBaseEnvOutsideAgentContext due environment/API base behavior, so full cli-core package verification is not green from this heartbeat. Grades: architecture B, security B, test coverage B, documentation C+, cross-platform C, signal B-, instrumentation B-. Measurement plan: add a cross-platform contract test or static validator that every scenario install.ps1 passing through cli-core includes -Manifest when the service manifest declares cli.freshness, and add/adjust cli-core PowerShell installer support so manifest freshness inputs/context match Unix install behavior.

Slice audited: lifecycle-internals (internal/lifecycle Runner start/stop/restart flow, scenario advisory locks, runtime registry start/stop sessions, health wait/reuse checks, Postgres bootstrap helpers, process-control shims, and focused lifecycle tests). Top finding: the stop path can leave lifecycle bookkeeping dirty when a port remains bound after kill attempts. Evidence: internal/lifecycle/lifecycle.go lines 680-691 calls killOrphansOnPorts, then returns immediately on verifyPortsReleased error at lines 684-685; only after that return site would it call r.Ports.RemoveScenarioLocks and runtimeStop.finish. verifyPortsReleased itself documents at lines 837-840 that partial stop should still continue to lock cleanup so a partial stop tears down everything it can. runtimeStop.finish in internal/lifecycle/runtime_registry.go lines 302-314 releases active runtime port claims and stops leases. Impact: a stuck listener after Stop/Restart can preserve legacy port lock files plus active runtime claims/leases, increasing retry noise and making later start/restart diagnosis look like registry or port-claim collision instead of the original stuck process. Coverage: tests exercise verifyPortsReleased happy/still-bound/eventually-free behavior and normal Stop registry finalization, but I found no contract test that a still-bound port still removes locks and releases/stops registry state. Measured checks: go test ./internal/lifecycle -run 'TestVerifyPortsReleased|TestAcquireScenarioLock' passed. Full go test ./internal/lifecycle failed in this sandbox before reaching behavioral assertions because registry-backed tests could not open the SQLite runtime database under VROOLI_SANDBOX_MERGED read-only mode, reporting 'unable to open database file: out of memory (14)'. Grades: architecture B, security B-, test coverage B, documentation B-, cross-platform C+, signal B, instrumentation B-. Measurement plan: add a stop-path contract test with a fake runtime store and persistent listeningPIDs that proves Stop returns a still-bound error while still removing scenario port locks and calling ReleaseActivePortClaimsForInstance/StopLease; then refactor cleanupScenarioRuntimeWithRegistry to collect verification errors and perform best-effort lock/registry cleanup before returning the aggregated error.
